• Login flow lives entirely on the server – no client‑side secrets.
• We set up a single‑sign‑on redirect URL that you control. | | User data protection | • Supabase’s Row‑Level Security (RLS) will automatically keep each user’s data private.
• No public tables or insecure reads. | | Email delivery | • If you have a commercial SMTP service (SendGrid, SES, etc.), we’ll use that, keeping the API key on the server only.

Who uses it: Anyone who visits the site and wants to sign in with their email. Risk level: Amber (because we’re handling personal email logins and data). Day‑one features: 1. User clicks “Sign in” → enters email. 2. Supabase sends a magic link (or one‑time code) to that address. 3. User clicks the link (or enters the code) → signed in. Information it stores: User email (and optional display name). No passwords, no other PII by default. Yes, private. Logins: Email‑only magic link (or code). No password storage. Money: None. Optionally prompt for a display name after first login. 7. Protect routes with `supabase.auth.getSession()` checks. 8. Save point before each step (e.g., commit “email‑login‑step‑1”).
